Black people looking like white people': your eleven are eleven of the valley's rolled people the fight already draws (the places' own, person_town_*), each his own body, his own skin and the face rendered off that same head; a name that reads a woman's wears a face with no beard; nobody else in the valley is dealt them)

night_lights.source: slices/fight_ground/fight_ground.json lights_key (COMBAT TWO 10/2, round twelve) and bb_all/1423_Nighttime (Status Effect).txt
night_lights.quote: a street lamp; live ones light a pool radius_m around their base (night: a lit tile plays as day)
night_lights.why: Battle Brothers' night is one status on everybody (-2 vision, -30% ranged skill, -30% ranged defence); our streets have lamps and burning drums, so the night is per tile: a man standing in a pool is seen at day range; a shooter takes the night's -30% only when his target stands in the dark; a target takes the night's -30% defence only when the shot comes out of the dark. Both lit is day, both dark is Battle Brothers' night exactly. The lesson: stay out of the light. No new number: the pool radius is COMBAT TWO's, the penalties the wiki's.

formation.quote: In the lower right corner of the inventory screen you now have three rows with 9 slots each. The lower row is your reserves; characters placed here do not take part in battle. The top two rows are your front and back battle lines, allowing you to place archers in the back and build a sturdy shieldwall in front.
formation.why: COMBAT [your formation] (Paolo's sixth votes: 'formation and gear are the depth'; GROK_75: 'the front line and the back line are already set by how you layered the company before the fight'). The fight opens with your men where the roster's two rows put them: slot 1 to 9 of the front row stand top to bottom on your front column, the back row one column behind. The roster order is RUN TWO's (FIGHT_OPTS.formation {front:[...], back:[...]}, crew indices or null); until its roster screen exists the default is Battle Brothers' own advice: the shieldwall in front, the shooters behind, in roster order, centred. Before turn one you may move any man to any tile of your two columns (ours: Battle Brothers sets this on the company screen; our roster screen is not built, so the fight hosts it); END TURN reads FIGHT and starts it; AUTO skips it.

enemy_tiers.source: bb_all/0299_Brigands.txt (the tactics), bb_all/0290_Brigand Leader.txt, bb_all/0293_Brigand Marauder.txt, bb_all/0297_Brigand Raider.txt, bb_all/0294_Brigand Marksman.txt (Bullseye after day 20); reference/library/grok/GROK_60_ENEMY_MATH_2026_10_02.md; bb_all/1409_Necromancer.txt (the mechanic's party: 'There is rarely more than one of them'), bb_all/0878_Goblins.txt, bb_all/1505_Orcs.txt
enemy_tiers.quote: In the early game Brigand groups usually consist of Thugs and sometimes Raiders. Later, Raiders become more common, ranged attackers appear and their numbers increase, and armored Marauders can spawn. In the late game you will usually see a Brigand Leader and other elite enemies among them. / Brigand Leaders start appearing in the middle game. Late game brigand groups usually have a Leader. It's rare to see simultaneously more than one. / Melee skill is 65 before day 40, 70 after. / (GROK_60) Combat difficulty, set at the start, raises both the count and the tier. Higher tier means more leaders and fewer thugs. Day scaling for those stops at day 100. A few is 2 to 3. Some is 4 to 6. / (Brigand Marksman) Ranged defense is 10 before day 40, 15 after.
enemy_tiers.why: COMBAT [the enemy math] (Paolo 10/5, rule 75b: 'the beginning is a lot different from the end'). The map hands the party (RUN [a few, not twelve]: the count, the days, the difficulty); the fight dresses it by tier. The phase boundaries are the wiki's own day gates (perks after day 20, the raider's skill after day 40, the marauder's best armour after day 60) and Grok's day 100 where roaming scaling stops; each combat difficulty above Veteran moves the tier as if the party were 20 days later (Beginner and Veteran the same); a party of 'some' (4) or more in the late phase brings its one leader. The mix weights are ours from the tactics paragraph; TUNING owns every one. A skill or a defence the wiki gives as a range (65-70, 10-15) is the before-and-after of skill_day, never a roll. THE BEASTS (COMBAT [the fight holds the grid], rule 117(e), 10/18): the pack's make-up is FACTIONS' draft for the lab-made beasts (records/target/bb/factions.json, faction beasts: early four dire wolves to two hyenas, late three dire wolves, two frenzied, one schrat); the middle phase keeps the early pack until a source says when the frenzied ones join; TUNING owns every weight.

first_week.quote: the starting kit, the first band and the tutorial fight are built around shooting / In the early game Brigand groups usually consist of Thugs and sometimes Raiders
first_week.why: THE FIRST BAND IS BUILT TO BE SHOT AT: the company's first week (days 1 to 7) meets thugs alone, the wiki's early band before its 'sometimes Raiders'; the lesser raider (75 health, 55 to 110 body armour) joins from day 8. Measured 10/19 before it: a fresh crew of three met two raiders in one band of three and lost every time, whatever it carried. The beasts' first week is their early pack. TUNING owns the day.

A pistol now SHOOTS from two tiles as Battle Brothers' own one-handed missile, the throwing class (range 2 to 4, Throw Javelin's 4 AP and 15 fatigue, +20 to hit and -10 a tile past two, its uses as the rounds it carries), each pistol riding the javelin row of its own price rank (the knife the crude javelins, the dagger and the notched blade the javelins, the rondel, the qatal and the estoc the heavy ones); at ONE tile it is the club its own row always was (Stab, Puncture). The shot's damage, armour and rounds are the javelin row's; its weight, price and name stay the pistol's. An enemy picks a pistol last (the wiki's early bands carry no shooters). THE ROUNDS ARE A MAGAZINE (10/19, measured: with five uses for the whole fight the company fired eleven shots a fight whatever the gap, and shooting could never be the main way it is won): the ridden row's uses are the rounds in the gun, and an empty pistol reloads them all with Battle Brothers' crossbow Reload (the light crossbow's row: 4 AP, its fatigue), only when it is empty (rule 117(b): one clear next thing). The rounds the company carries between fights are ECONOMY's [the first bullets].

Both sides: an enemy's crossbow is a rifle too. It holds no ring (rule 103: a gun in his hands holds none).

weapon_says_weak.quote: the game doesn't explain to you at all that your weapon sucks / before a shot or a swing, under the finger, the hit chance and what it does to that target's armour, and one plain line when the weapon is bad for it ('your pipe barely dents his plate'); after it, what it did
weapon_says_weak.why: the one plain line comes up when the arm in his hand needs this many body blows or more to drop the man he aims at, his armour wearing down blow by blow (the fight's own damage math at the weapon's middle damage, FIGHT.preview). Measured 10/19 over the company's six arms: a fresh crew drops a day-one thug in 2 to 4 blows (no line: the first fight is not a lecture), a pistol needs 5 for a lesser raider, everything but the sledge 8 to 21 for a leader or a marauder in plate. When a man of his drops that one in fewer, the line names him. TUNING owns the number.

beast_rig_looks.source: slices/fight_rig/fight_rig.json (COMBAT [the fight wears the 3D models], tools/bohemia_combat_the_fight_wears_the_rig.py): ANIMATION's redone dire wolf, cave hyena and feral shepherd through DIRECTION's master rig
beast_rig_looks.quote: BRO EVERYTHING IS A 3D MODEL NOW FUCK THE UGLY 8 BIT SHIT... WTF TRYING TO COMBINE THE TWO

act_weights.quote: maybe they're way more around for the first act than the third act; there's gonna be enemy types around more in different acts than another, that's just how it is
act_weights.why: COMBAT [ghosts and apparitions] 10/23: every enemy type the fight can field carries a weight for each of the three acts (act one, two, three); the fight multiplies a party's mix by the act it is told (FIGHT_OPTS.act, act one when none), and the map's spawner reads the same row to choose which parties walk (RUN, WORLD). Ghosts three times as often in act one, as often as anything in act two, a quarter in act three: they are the Amalgamation's haunting as act one sees it (rule 134(e)), and by acts two and three people know what they are. The numbers are a draft (tuned: false): TUNING owns them.
act_weights.bestiary: COMBAT [bestiary] 10/24 (rule 134(b): 'every enemy type carries a weight per act'): THE MECHANIC's machines grow as the world gets its tech back (1 / 1.5 / 2: the future is reclaimed and techy, his second votes); THE KIDS AND RUNNERS are the ruin's children (1.5 / 1 / 0.5: fewer once the towns hold); THE HEAVY needs a working suit (0.5 / 1 / 1.5). Drafts; TUNING owns them.

graveyard.source: VAMILY.md rule 134(a) (Paolo 10/23: 'like in Battle Brothers, one of the enemies are ghosts and apparitions; I think we can put that in, it fits our world too good'): 'a place full of them is our graveyard'; 134(b) more in act one, fewer by act three; Woodlawn Cemetery, Las Vegas (1914): sections of upright stones in rows, aisles between sections, the old families' crypts and obelisks
graveyard.quote: a place full of them is our graveyard
graveyard.why: COMBAT 10/24 [ghosts and apparitions]: the cemetery (WORLD's district 'cemetery', or a fight told place 'graveyard') is dealt on the valley's open scrub (no twin beside its twin) and dressed with the field: one row of headstones a tile (one piece of cover there), an aisle every aisle_every columns, a path across path_row, the crypt (it blocks a step) and the obelisks on field tiles, the fresh graves in the bottom fresh_rows_from_bottom rows; each line's own open_cols_each_line columns stay open to stand in. A row's foot stands at foot_m (metres into its tile, across and down). The band is the place's own: the ghosts faction, crowd times the handed party (or the company's own line, fallback_band_by_company), times the Geist's act weight over act one's (3 / 1 / 0.25: the graveyard full in act one, one ghost by act three). MEASURED 10/24 (AUTO, 40 seeds a cell, on the graveyard): 3 men beat 2 ghosts 90%, 3 ghosts 40%, 5 ghosts 0%; 6 men beat 5 ghosts 50%, 6 ghosts 35%, 9 ghosts 0%; 12 men beat 11 ghosts 78%, 12 ghosts 83%, 18 ghosts 0%. A crowd of 2 (twice the crew) is a graveyard no company leaves; crowd 1 is the hardest fight on the line (rule 133(b): hardcore if you mess around), and the lesson (walk up and hit it) is the way through. TUNING owns the numbers.

bestiary.source: records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_BESTIARY_COUNT_9_29_26.md (the 9/29 draft; NECROMANCER -> THE MECHANIC is marked his words); VAMILY.md COMBAT [bestiary]
bestiary.quote: NECROMANCER -> THE MECHANIC (his words): a man who keeps reviving his robots; kill him and the machines drop.
bestiary.why: COMBAT [bestiary] 10/24: the names the board and the feed call each new kind (draft:true for WORDS), and THE MECHANIC's one rule that is ours and not Battle Brothers': when the last mechanic falls, every machine he kept running drops where it stands and never gets up (in Battle Brothers the undead fight on). The lesson in one meeting: kill him first.

road_factions.source: VAMILY.md rule 75 (Paolo 10/5, THE ORIGIN SETS THE COMPANY, AND THE ROAD SETS THE ENEMY) and rule 134(b) (Paolo 10/23); records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_BESTIARY_COUNT_9_29_26.md
road_factions.quote: there's gonna be enemy types around more in different acts than another, that's just how it is

From his second fight on, a party handed as brigands is one of the valley's factions, drawn by the act it is fought in (the same weights as act_weights: the kids the ruin's, the machines and the heavies the reclaimed future's); his first fight stays brigands (the lessons of the first fight). A party the map names with its own faction (ghosts, beasts) keeps it. The day the map's parties carry their faction (RUN, WORLD), this table is the spawner's and the fight stops rolling. outclass.source: VAMILY.md rule 143(b) (Paolo 10/24); records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_SPANGLISH_TEN_PERCENT_THE_WIPE_THE_COMMENTARY_AND_THE_MAP_10_24_26.md; his level from rules.json parsed.brother_xp (bb_all/1316_Morale.txt: XP value of a brother is 100 + 30 * (his level - 1)), the same worth scale every enemy row carries as xp
outclass.quote: when everyone dies in a match it's kind of hard to understand... an enemy just kept dodging all of my bullets, I don't know how we can make it clear visually that the enemy is superior
outclass.why: COMBAT [the loss is understood] 10/24: an enemy reads LV n, his level on Battle Brothers' own worth scale (1 + (xp - 100) / 30, the brother formula run backwards); he OUTCLASSES YOU when that level is level_gap or more over the best man of yours still standing, or when he both dodges (the best man of yours, skill against his defence alone, hits him dodge_chance_at_most in 100 or less) and is armoured (the arm of yours that drops him fastest needs blows_at_least blows or more, weapon_says_weak's count); a shot he dodges throws him aside for dodge_lean_beats of a beat. Drafts for TUNING, tuned:false.

wipe.quote: when I die it was very hard to tell what happened next... if everyone in the party dies or gets down you're still where you were before you entered the battle and it just feels clunky... literally your whole squad got wiped, that's pretty important
wipe.why: COMBAT [the loss is understood] 10/24: the wipe's beat on the board before the recap: the head at once, then one line of what happened a beat (beats_per_line), the last line what comes next, held hold_beats; at 120 BPM a five-line wipe reads in five seconds, then the recap's own four beats. Drafts for TUNING, tuned:false.

odds_colour.source: VAMILY.md rule 144(b)(e)(f)(g) (Paolo 10/24); amends 141(a)'s 'letting me know your percentage'
odds_colour.quote: I wouldn't press AUTO unless I'm guaranteed none of my members would die... maybe we don't show the percentages, a number in the background the player never sees, they only see the colour... varying levels of the colour on a scale, not five colours... if any members die during your projections, then that's leaning towards red... I don't want clear; if it's clear, could go either way, that means it's gonna be risky
odds_colour.why: COMBAT [the auto button wears the odds] 10/24: each of the 24 runs played out from the board as it stands is worth 1 won with nobody down or dead, down_value x the share still standing when won with men down and none dead, 0 lost or with any death; the worth's mean is the hidden number. At or over turn the AUTO tin is tinted green, under it red, each side from alpha_min (never clear) to alpha_max at its end (readable in the sun); the beat's light only at glow_at or over (and one tap then finishes the fight, as before). A fight that is merely even (0.5) reads red. Drafts for TUNING, tuned:false.

gore.quote: when an enemy gets hurt, or even your own player, I want them to turn slightly faint red opacity, and then I wanna see blood come out, maybe blood splatters too... if an enemy gets down he might fall on the ground, a pile of blood underneath him
gore.why: COMBAT [a hit shows, the ground remembers] 10/24: the man hit flashes red at flash_alpha fading over flash_beats; a hit throws one drop per hp_per_drop of health it took, drops_min to drops_max, each landing as a stain that stays (the last stains_kept kept, a whole long fight); a pool spreads under the fallen over pool_beats. Drafts for TUNING, tuned:false.

sight.quote: if there are tiles that our team, with their vision all together, can't see, you've gotta be able to tell; a different opacity, maybe a grey darkness to it... it's gotta be done a lot better
sight.why: COMBAT [what the crew can't see reads dark] 10/24: a tile none of his men sees wears dark at dark_alpha with a static of light specks (static_density of its cells) at static_alpha over it, lifting or falling over lift_beats; a man of theirs lost from sight leaves a rust ring at lost_alpha[0] fading to lost_alpha[1] over lost_beats, until seen again. per_level: the library says height adds vision toward lower ground ('Elevation is taken into account after the cap... applied only vs lower positioned opponents') and names no number: one tile a level.

roof_storeys.source: VAMILY.md rule 164 item 14 (Paolo 10/24, records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_PC_PLAYTEST_AND_THE_TWENTY_DOLLARS_10_24_26.md); the library: bb_all/0424_Combat Mechanics.txt (four height levels, 0 to 3) and 1002_Hit Chance.txt; the faces measured on COMBAT TWO's block art (slices/fight_ground/block_*.webp, the 45 law: a face is its height x cos45 at 42.9 px a metre)
roof_storeys.quote: one-story versus two-story or even a three-story building, I don't know how that helps me and it's hard to tell visually
roof_storeys.why: COMBAT [the PC playtest: the fight's part] (3) 10/25: a roof you can stand on (a 'height' tile of a building block, roof_kinds) is Battle Brothers' height level = its storeys (its face in metres / metres_per_storey, rounded, at least 1, at most 3); blocks lists the roof tiles over one storey as [x, y, storeys] inside the 5 x 5 block; every other height tile is level 1 (a one-storey roof, a rise of ground, a trash heap). What the level does is the library's, unchanged. rise: how far up the tile (a share of a tile's height on the glass) a man on that level stands, so he stands on his roof's plane (drawing only). not_roofs: a height tile inside a roof block that the art draws as bare ground (works.0's 1,4, in front of the low works), a rise of ground: level 1, no ladder.

bag.source: VAMILY.md rule 164 item 15 (Paolo 10/24, records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_PC_PLAYTEST_AND_THE_TWENTY_DOLLARS_10_24_26.md); the library: rules ap.swap_item, ap.bag_slots, fatigue.bag_items_penalty_multiplier; perks quick_hands, bags_and_belts
bag.quote: you can't switch weapon... Battle Brothers has two slots to bring shit into combat... it takes up stamina
bag.why: COMBAT [the PC playtest: the fight's part] (4) 10/25: a man carries what the crew screen put in his two bag slots (gear.bag, item ids, RUN TWO's hand-over; four with Bags and Belts) and swaps it into his hands for the library's 4 AP (Quick Hands: the first swap a turn free); what rides in the bag weighs on his wind at half its weight (Bags and Belts: only a two-hander's). kit: until the crew screen hands a bag, a man with none carries this by his weapon's job (a pistol man the pipe, everybody else a pistol: guns lead, rule 120), so the swap is there in the first fight; a handed bag, even an empty one, wins.
